overall: Board violated the Open Meeting Law by creating insufficient minutes for its August 3 and 31, 2022 meetings; minutes approved earlier were untimely and not reviewed. Orders: compliance, amend minutes, training.

allegations.summary: Complaint says Board minutes omit votes on ARPA fund allocations; most minutes were approved more than 30 days before the complaint was filed.
allegations.key_passage: All but two sets of minutes were approved more than 30 days prior to the date the complaint was filed with the Board; therefore, the complaint is untimely with respect to those meeting minutes, and we decline to review their sufficiency.

allegations.summary: Complaint says the August 3 and 31 minutes lack substantive discussion summaries, meeting location, and lists of documents used, violating the minutes requirements.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons stated above, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by creating insufficient minutes for its meetings held on August 3 and 31.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.

Within 30 days of the letter, amend the August 3 and 31 minutes to include summaries of all discussions, the location of each meeting, and a list of documents used at each meeting, and certify compliance in writing to the AG's office.
All Board members must attend an Open Meeting Law training webinar within 90 days of receiving the letter.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
